name: Isolated Spontaneous Cervical Artery Dissection

criteria.description: Radiological evidence of arterial wall hematoma or intimal flap on MRI, MRA, CTA, or catheter angiography
Acute onset of focal neurological symptoms consistent with ischemia in the territory of the dissected artery
No history of recent significant cervical trauma or iatrogenic injury
Presence of ipsilateral neck pain or headache preceding neurological symptoms

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Imaging confirmation plus clinical presentation with absence of trauma
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on imaging combined with clinical features; exclusion of traumatic causes is essential.

pathognomonic.notes: Partial Horner syndrome due to sympathetic chain involvement
searchTerms: same side drooping eyelid and small pupil
unequal pupil and eyelid droop on one side

pathognomonic.symptomName: Ipsilateral neck pain localized to carotid or vertebral artery
searchTerms: one-sided neck pain near carotid artery
localized neck pain on one side

pathognomonic.symptomName: Focal cerebral ischemic symptoms (e.g., transient ischemic attack or stroke)

searchTerms: pulsing ringing in ear on same side

common.symptomName: Transient visual disturbances (amaurosis fugax or diplopia)
Cranial nerve palsies (e.g., lower cranial nerves IX-XII)
searchTerms: paralysis of throat and tongue nerves

occasional.symptomName: Neck swelling or palpable cervical mass
Nausea and vomiting associated with posterior circulation ischemia
searchTerms: nausea and vomiting with brainstem stroke
sick feeling with brain blood flow issues

rare.symptomName: Subarachnoid hemorrhage due to arterial rupture
searchTerms: bleeding around brain from artery rupture
brain hemorrhage due to artery burst

rare.symptomName: Hearing loss due to labyrinthine artery involvement
searchTerms: hearing loss from inner ear artery damage
hearing problems due to ear blood flow loss

laboratory: Coagulation profile to exclude hypercoagulable states
imaging: MRI/MRA showing intramural hematoma or double lumen
CT angiography demonstrating arterial stenosis or pseudoaneurysm
Catheter angiography as gold standard for vessel lumen abnormalities
genetic: No specific genetic markers identified; connective tissue disorders (e.g., Ehlers-Danlos syndrome) may predispose
other: Clinical exclusion of trauma or iatrogenic causes
Blood pressure monitoring for hypertension as risk factor

distinguishingFeatures: History of recent neck trauma or manipulation
Imaging findings consistent with traumatic injury
Systemic symptoms such as fever and weight loss
Temporal artery tenderness or biopsy confirmation
Characteristic 'string of beads' appearance on angiography

redFlags: Sudden onset of focal neurological deficits
Signs of subarachnoid hemorrhage or arterial rupture
references: Debette S, Leys D. Cervical-artery dissections: predisposing factors, diagnosis, and outcome. Lancet Neurol. 2009 Jul;8(7):668-78.
Schievink WI. Spontaneous dissection of the carotid and vertebral arteries. N Engl J Med. 2001 Mar 22;344(12):898-906.
Orphanet: Isolated spontaneous cervical artery dissection (ORPHA:689001)
